# Scope

# Purpose
A kit (or pack) is one product you sell that is made of several items — for example, a 5-pack of boys' t-shirts in one bag.
This feature lets the costing team work out how much one kit costs to make: the garments inside it, the packaging, the labour, and any extra charges like freight.
The user then types in a selling price, and the screen shows the profit.
When everyone agrees on the numbers, the kit is approved and locked so nobody can change it.
To price the same kit in other sizes, the user can duplicate it — one copy per size — instead of building each one from scratch.

# Solution

## Words used in this document

[TABLE 1: Table 1 · 11 rows · columns: Term (text), What it means (text) · identifiers: Term]
| Term | What it means |
| Kit / Pack | One sellable product made of several items. Its Component Type is either "Multi (Kit)" or "Single (Pack)". |
| BOM | "Bill of Materials" — the full list of everything that goes into the kit. |
| Master kit | The original kit that other kits were copied from. |
| Child kit | A copy of a master kit made for one specific size. It stays linked to its master. |
| Family | A master kit plus all of its child kits. |
| Ratio Type | Decides how items are broken down. Color Ratio: one size, many colours. Size Ratio: one colour, many sizes. |
| Wastage % | Extra material allowed for loss or damage. 2% wastage on 100 bags means you pay for 102. |
| Total Cost | Everything added up: items + packaging + labour + extra charges. |
| Profit % (Margin) | How much of the selling price is profit. |
| Markup % | How much the selling price is above the cost. |
| Open / Approved | The two statuses a kit can have. Open = still being worked on. Approved = final and locked. |

## Step by Step Working
• Create the kit. Click "Configure Kit/Pack", fill in the basic details (name, SKU, buyer, season and so on) and click "Create Kit".
• Add the items. On the Pack Items tab, add each garment and choose its colours or sizes. Enter quantity and price.
• Add packaging. On the Packing Materials tab, add bags, tickets, labels and so on.
• Add labour. On the Routing/Processes tab, pick the packing process and its rate.
• Add extra charges. On the Additional Cost tab, add things like freight.
• Check the totals. On the Summary tab, see the total cost, type in the selling price, and check the profit.
• Make size versions (optional). From the list, duplicate the kit into other sizes.
• Approve. Click "Approve". The kit is now locked.
• Auto Save. is also working.

## Kit/Pack Screens

### 3.1 Kit list (Kit/Pack Management)
It is the starting page. It shows every kit. Child kits appear indented under their master kit.
List will have column as Kit SKU & SKU description.
The kit list. Child kits (like KIT-382) sit under their master (KIT-381).
List will have a column name Image where we will show image of the Kit/Pack and the same will be seen inside Kit/pack page, at the header level will show a image & from there we can attach the image as well.
Actions that can be done-
• Search by Kit ID, name or SKU. If a child kit matches, its master kit is shown too, so you can see where it belongs.
• Create a new kit with the "Configure Kit/Pack" button.
• Open a kit by clicking its Kit ID.
• Use the ⋮ menu at the end of each row for more actions (see below).
The ⋮ row menu on a master kit

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 1 rows · columns: Menu option (text), When you see it (text), What it does (text)]
| Menu option | When you see it | What it does |
| Duplicate | Master kits only | Makes copies of the kit for other sizes. |
Columns in the list
Kit (ID and name), Kit SKU, SKU Description, Component Type, Ratio Type, UOM, BOM Status, Total Cost, Created By, Created On and Last Modified. Most columns can be filtered, and all can be sorted.

### 3.2 Duplicate pop-up
Use Case: making size versions of a kit quickly. Pick one or more sizes, and the system creates one new child kit for each size.
Duplicate pop-up: pick one or more sizes
Working:
• If the Ratio type is Size Ratio then while duplicating it will show colors to select, if Color Ratio then while duplicating it will show sizes to select & if Mixed ratio then while duplicating it will show colors & sizes to be selected. Multi- selection of colors & sizes is allowed.
• The size list shows the sizes already used in the kit (or XS to XXL if there are none yet). Sizes that already have a child kit are hidden, so you can't create the same size twice.
• Each new kit gets the next free Kit ID and is named "{master name} - {size}", for example "Boys Tee Kit - L".
• Everything is copied from the master: items, packaging, labour and extra charges. Only the chosen size is kept on the items.
• The new kit starts fresh: status is Open, actual quantity is 0, and you are recorded as its creator.
• A child kit cannot be duplicated again. Only one level of copying is allowed.

### 3.3 Kit detail page
Use Case: building and pricing one kit. The page has six tabs. The top of the page shows the kit name, its status, the expected and actual order quantity, the currency, and — for a child kit — which master it was copied from.

#### Tab 1 — Kit/Pack (basic details)
Kit/Pack tab with the kit's basic details
UOM and Folder fields should be driven from user profile there we need a section name Kit/Pack on User Profile.

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 11 rows · columns: Field (text), Required? (text), Rules (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Required? | Rules |
| Packing Kit ID | Automatic | Created by the system. You can't edit it. |
| Packing Kit Name | Yes | Up to 120 characters |
| Kit SKU | Yes | Up to 60 characters |
| SKU Description | No | Up to 250 characters |
| Component Type | Yes | Single (Pack) or Multi (Kit) |
| Ratio Type | Yes | Color Ratio or Size Ratio (see Tab 2) |
| Product Group, Sub-Category | Yes | Pick from list |
| UOM (unit) | Yes | As per defined User Profile |
| Order Qty Expected | Yes | A whole number above 0. Starts as 1. |
| Buyer, Buyer Dept, Season | Yes | Pick from list |
| Packing Kit Description | No | Up to 2,000 characters |
There is also a "Copy From" button, it will show previous made Kits/packs and will create a new kit (not to be seen as duplicate Kit/Pack).

#### Tab 2 — Pack Items (the garments)
Each main row is one item, such as a t-shirt. Under it, the system automatically creates one row for every colour-and-size combination you pick. You enter the quantity and price on those rows.
The Ratio Type decides what you can pick:
• Color Ratio — one size for the whole kit, but many colours.
• Size Ratio — one colour for the whole kit, but many sizes.
Pack Items: the t-shirt row, with its Black / L row underneath

[TABLE 4: Table 4 · 6 rows · columns: Column (text), Where (text), Rules (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Where | Rules |
| Article Code, Article Name | Main row | Free text |
| Color, Size | Main row (you pick) / Sub-row (shown only) | — |
| Quantity, Price | Sub-row | 0 or more, 2 decimals |
| Cons. UOM (unit) | Sub-row | Free text |
| Value | Both | Quantity × Price (automatic) |
| Manufacturing BOM | Main row | Free text |

#### Tab 3 — Packing Materials (the packaging)
A simple list of packaging items such as poly bags and price tickets. Click "Add Article" to add a row.
Packing Materials: a poly bag and a price ticket
Packing Material Tab should have currency.
Colour & Size should not be mandatory for packing material (If blank should be considered as None type dependency).

[TABLE 5: Table 5 · 7 rows · columns: Column (text), Rules (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Rules |
| Article Code, Article Name | Free text |
| Material Color, Material Size | Optional — shows "None" if left blank |
| Cons. Qty, Wastage % | 0 or more, 2 decimals |
| Supplier, Delivery Term, Cons. UOM, Purchase UOM | Free text |
| Currency | Pick from list (packaging can be priced in a different currency) |
| Cons. UOM Price, Purchase Price | 0 or more, 2 decimals |
| Value | Automatic: Qty × (1 + Wastage %) × Price |

#### Tab 4 — Routing/Processes (labour)
Just two fields: pick one process (Packing 1, Packing 2, Ironing, Folding or Labelling) and enter its rate. Clearing the process also clears the rate.

#### Tab 5 — Additional Cost (extra charges)
A list of extra charges like freight. Each charge is either a fixed amount or a percentage. Percentages are always worked out on the cost of items + packaging + labour, so the order of the rows doesn't matter.
Additional Cost: a freight charge of 25,000

[TABLE 6: Table 6 · 5 rows · columns: Column (text), Rules (text) · identifiers: Column]
| Column | Rules |
| Charges | Free text, e.g. "Freight Charges" |
| Basis | Amount or Percentage |
| Currency | Free text (should become a pick list — see Known issues #7) |
| Rate | 0 or more, 2 decimals |
| Value | Automatic: the amount itself, or the percentage of the subtotal |

#### Tab 6 — Summary (totals and profit)
A view-only overview of the whole kit, plus the place to enter the selling price.
Summary: kit info, every cost line, and the totals
• Kit Information — kit ID, name, component type and ratio type.
• BOM Line Items — one line per item, packaging material, labour and extra charge.
• Totals — Total Cost, Selling Price (you type this), Discount % (you type this, but it doesn't affect anything yet), Profit %, Markup %, and BMV and EPM (always 0.00 for now).
• Approval Summary — on master kits only. Shows the master and all its child kits in one table.
Approval Summary on a master kit: KIT-381 and its child KIT-382
Approval summary Column- Kit, Kit- SKU, Kit-SKU Description, BOM Status, Total Cost, Selling Price/FOB, Profit %, Markup%, EMP.

## Messages the user will see
These must appear exactly as written.

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 14 rows · columns: When (text), Title (text), Message (text) · identifiers: When]
| When | Title | Message |
| Deleting a kit (no children) | Confirm Deletion | {PackingKitID} will be deleted. This cannot be undone. |
| Deleting a master with children | Confirm Deletion | {PackingKitID} and its {N} duplicated child kit(s) will be deleted. This cannot be undone. |
| Delete worked | Deleted | {PackingKitID} was deleted. |
| Delete failed | Delete Failed | Could not delete the Kit/Pack. |
| List didn't load | Load Failed | Could not load Kit/Packs from the mock store. |
| One size duplicated | Kit Duplicated | {newID} was created from {masterID}. |
| Several sizes duplicated | Kits Duplicated | {N} kits created from {masterID}: {id, id, …}. |
| Duplicate failed | Duplicate Failed | Could not create the duplicate Kit/Pack(s). |
| Required fields missing | Cannot Create Kit | Fill in every required field first (Name, Kit SKU, Component Type, Ratio Type, Product Group, Sub-Category, UOM, Buyer, Buyer Dept, Season). |
| Kit created | Kit Created | {PackingKitID} was created. |
| Create failed | Create Failed | Could not create the Kit/Pack. |
| Auto-save failed | Save Failed | Could not save the Kit/Pack. |
| Kit doesn't exist | Not Found | That Kit/Pack does not exist. (then returns to the list) |
| "Copy From" clicked | Not Available Yet | Copying an existing Kit/Pack is not built in this proto yet. |
